ambient_trade.text: Wool bales going for 40 gold in {town} this week. Fair weight, no clipping :)
Salt is selling at {gold} a sack in {town}. Anyone bound for the Pellegrane road, now is the time to buy.
Buying good hides in {town}, paying {gold} on the spot. Fair dealing, as always.
Caravan leaving {town} at dawn with spare room for two carts. Share the road fee and we both save.
Quick sales on dyed cloth in {town}. Name a price within reason and I will meet you halfway.

encounter_trade_offer.text: Ser {player}, I do not trade with raiders, but {gold} for the salt at {town} is a fair number. Speak plainly if you want it.
Ser {player}, {gold} for the wool delivered to {town}? That is a fair offer and I will take it if the weight holds.
Ah, {player}, you have a nose for profit! {gold} for the whole lot in {town} and we both walk away richer. Shake on it?

encounter_greeting.text: Stay back, {player}. This is {persona} of {my_faction}, and my wagons are not for raiders.
Good day, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}, traveling the Pellegrane road. Nothing to fear here unless you carry a toll receipt I am missing.
{player}! {persona} of {my_faction} here. Fancy meeting you on the road. Any salt to spare, or are you only passing through with empty carts?

player_raided_my_village.text: {player} burned {village} and I lost three carts of wool to the smoke. Every fire you light costs the whole road money.
Ser {player}, {village} is ash now. Name your price for the damages and we can talk business instead of blades.
Raids on {village} cost us all a fortune in lost wool, {player}. Ledger is open and I am keeping score.
{player}, the burning of {village} was bad for trade on everyone's road. Let us settle it with coin before the bandits notice.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} is at war with {enemy_faction}. Good for the swordsmiths, terrible for the rest of us with carts on the road.
War with {enemy_faction} means tolls on every bridge will climb by midsummer. Someone explain the logic to me, please.
Fine, {my_faction} has declared on {enemy_faction}. My wool prices are already rising and my patience is shorter than my margins.
Caravans bound for {enemy_faction} lands are suspended until further notice. Buy your salt early, the road will be dear.
{enemy_faction} and {my_faction} at each other's throats again. Stock up now, because in a war prices only climb.

peace_made.text: Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last. Roads reopen and my drivers can sleep again. Very good news.
Finally, {my_faction} has made peace with {faction}. Expect cheaper salt on the Pellegrane road by the next market day.
Terms agreed between {my_faction} and {faction}. I have already booked three caravans for the reopened routes.
Ink is dry on the treaty with {faction}. Wool, bread and salt move freely again, and I can finally stop counting tolls in my sleep.

released_by_player.text: Thank you, {player}, for letting me go without a ransom. I will remember the courtesy, and maybe the next wool shipment too.
{player}, you let me walk free instead of asking for gold. That is a rare kind of deal and I will return the favor on the road.
{player} released me without ransom. A strange choice, but I will not complain. A free cart is a good cart.
{player}, you spared me the ransom. Do not think this makes us friends, but I owe you one and I always pay my debts.

beat_by_player.text: {player} beat us in the field with {troop_count} troops. Forty good men lost on bad ground. Expensive lesson, that.
{player}, your {troop_count} men caught my escort in the open. Good fight, fair fight. I will be more careful on the Pellegrane road.
Well played, {player}. Your {troop_count} troops got the better of mine today. I will buy you a drink the next time we trade.
You won this one, {player}, with {troop_count} men against my lot. Do not expect me to thank you for it, but I will count the cost.
{player} took the field with {troop_count} troops and beat us fair. I still want my wagons back, but I respect the win.

whisper_beg_help.text: {player}, {enemy_faction} is pressing on {fief} and my caravans are stuck behind it. Can you spare a few men? I will pay well.
My friend {player}, {fief} is under threat from {enemy_faction}. Help me hold it and the next salt shipment is yours at cost.
{player}, I need your swords at {fief} before {enemy_faction} takes the bridge. Name a fair price and I will meet it.
{player}, {enemy_faction} will strangle the road to {fief} if we do nothing. Would you ride with me? Bread and wool are at stake.

ambient_complaint.text: Tolls at {town} jumped overnight. Bandits eat my profits, then the toll keeper eats what is left.
{rival} undercut my salt price again in {town}. That is not trade, it is charity, and charity does not pay the carts.
Another wagon hit by bandits on the hill road outside {town}. Still waiting for the guard to show up and earn their pay.
{faction} merchants are flooding the market with cheap cloth. Fine for buyers, painful for every honest wool seller on the road.
Hauling wool costs more than it earns this season. Someone tell {rival} that cheap hauling is not the same as fair pricing.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain again on the Pellegrane road. My wool is soaked and my temper is damp :)
Anyone heading out of {town} with spare cart space? Share the escort and split the road fees.
The harvest in {village} came in heavy this year. Good for bread, better for a clever trader who buys early.
Lag is eating my caravan timers again. I can see the carts moving but the trade window keeps freezing, xD
Sold every sack of salt I brought to {town} before lunch. Good prices and a little luck, I suppose.
